chapter: Changing styles, the road and nightlife
title: Earl Hines's bus accident and road dangers
summary: They recall the 1935 crash that killed Cecil Irwin, with Lester Young filling in, and the cost of touring today.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: The road's always been tough. Quinn Wilson told me about the accident Earl Hines' band had, in '35 or something like that, where one of the guys was killed, and --
And they had to go ahead and play the job then.
Said Lester Young -- they were up in Minnesota, I guess. And Lester Young filled in....
Oh, yeah, right. I never knew who filled in for him, right.
But those were the conditions with the bands in that time, and they -- all of the band and all of the musicians, black musicians, it wasn't too, too, kosher
And it's still bad, the road, guys getting killed and --

Oh, yeah, right. Well, the conditions on the road are bad. If they have to travel that way, it's according to how they travel, but with the big bands, with the exorbitant fees for busses and things now, a lot of them travel by cars and things.
